fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Pulmonary optimization before elective incisional-hernia repair
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: For a stable adult with a reducible, nonemergent incisional hernia and poorly controlled COPD, select pulmonary optimization before finalizing elective repair.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Initial imaging of a palpable breast mass under age 30
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select targeted breast ultrasound as the initial imaging study for the scoped adult patient younger than 30 with a new palpable breast mass.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Management of an asymptomatic simple breast cyst
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select no cyst-directed procedure for an imaging-concordant simple breast cyst that is not painful or bothersome.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Initial treatment of a painful simple breast cyst
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Offer needle aspiration for symptom relief from a persistently painful or bothersome, imaging-concordant simple breast cyst.
Recognize canonical EBV-associated malignancies while preserving the boundary that an association is neither universal across every tumor nor an individual cancer-risk prediction.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Apply standard Milan criteria to HCC referral
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Apply standard Milan tumor-number, size, macrovascular-invasion, and extrahepatic-disease criteria to recognize when HCC tumor burden supports transplant-center evaluation without treating the criteria as automatic listing.
Recognize the characteristic superficial breast or chest-wall venous cord and its underlying superficial thrombophlebitis.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Selective imaging evaluation of suspected Mondor disease
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select targeted Doppler ultrasound when the superficial venous diagnosis is uncertain and age-appropriate diagnostic breast imaging when focal symptoms require evaluation for underlying pathology.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Supportive management of uncomplicated Mondor disease
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Use supportive care for concordant uncomplicated Mondor disease while recognizing findings that require renewed evaluation.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Female sex and perioperative mortality after elective AAA repair
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Recognize that women have higher observed perioperative mortality after elective intact AAA repair at the group level, while preserving the boundary that this association does not determine an individual outcome or select a repair approach.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Initial active surveillance for selected desmoid tumors
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Choose specialist active surveillance as the initial strategy for newly diagnosed, stable or minimally symptomatic desmoid disease without critical threat or meaningful functional deterioration.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Surgical option for progressing symptomatic abdominal-wall desmoid
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Recognize function-preserving resection after multidisciplinary review as an option for progressing symptomatic abdominal-wall desmoid when expected morbidity is acceptably low.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Distal pancreatectomy with splenectomy for resectable tail adenocarcinoma
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select oncologic distal pancreatectomy with splenectomy when a fit patient with pancreatic-tail adenocarcinoma has been judged resectable and is proceeding to surgery.
Recognize Felty syndrome from rheumatoid arthritis with persistent neutropenia, usually with splenomegaly, after important alternative causes have been excluded.
Select specialist-monitored methotrexate as the usual first-line disease-modifying treatment and distinguish bridging therapy from the long-term plan.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Splenectomy for medically refractory Felty syndrome
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Consider splenectomy only after recurrent infections persist despite adequate medical therapy and multidisciplinary review.
Order paired 24-hour urine and serum calcium-creatinine measurements before parathyroid localization when FHH is suspected.
Use relative hypocalciuria, family context, and appropriate genetic evaluation without treating a low clearance ratio as independently diagnostic.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Avoid unnecessary parathyroid surgery in FHH
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Reassure and observe a patient with confirmed uncomplicated FHH rather than performing routine parathyroid surgery.
Recognize acute lymphangitis from a distal skin entry site, a tender erythematous streak extending proximally, and tender regional lymph nodes.
Select the owner-approved initial management category for a completed incidental gallbladder-polyp ultrasound profile.
For the approved resectable distal common-bile-duct profile, select hospital HPB referral for pancreaticoduodenectomy and distinguish the represented distal location.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Obstructive jaundice, vitamin K, and coagulopathy
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Recognize the approved relationship between obstructive jaundice, reduced vitamin K absorption, and vitamin K-related coagulopathy.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: HCC resection selection in compensated cirrhosis
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: For the approved favorable compensated-cirrhosis profile, select hospital HPB-surgery referral for hepatic resection evaluation without treating Child-Pugh A status or Milan classification alone as sufficient.
Recognize the splenic hilum as the most common location represented for an accessory spleen without treating one location as a complete splenectomy plan.
For the approved persistent-hemolysis presentation after total splenectomy, reassess and evaluate for functioning accessory splenic tissue without relying on MCV, RDW, or Howell-Jolly bodies alone.
For confirmed functioning accessory splenic tissue causing persistent symptomatic hemolysis, refer to hospital surgery for removal without treating incidental tissue as an indication.
Identify pouchitis as the approved common inflammatory pouch complication after IPAA for ulcerative colitis.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Type IVA congenital bile duct cyst anatomy
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Identify Type IVA as the approved combined intrahepatic and extrahepatic cystic-dilatation pattern.
Identify high-risk human papillomavirus as the approved etiologic association of anal HSIL.
Recognize the approved MEN2A pattern of medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, and primary hyperparathyroidism.
Recognize that a functioning pheochromocytoma must be excluded or addressed before thyroid intervention in the approved MEN2A scope.
When both are indicated for a functioning pheochromocytoma, establish alpha blockade before adding beta blockade.
Recognize the characteristic soft, yellowish, deformable subepithelial phenotype of a colonic lipoma while preserving the boundary that an absent cushion sign does not exclude it.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Management of a clearly characterized asymptomatic colonic lipoma
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Choose no lipoma-directed treatment or dedicated surveillance for a clearly characterized asymptomatic colonic lipoma and recognize features that make that pathway inapplicable.
Identify vitamin C as a cofactor for proline and lysine hydroxylation in collagen biosynthesis and connect inadequate hydroxylation with reduced collagen stability and impaired healing.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Pathologic recognition of gastric MALT lymphoma
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Recognize gastric MALT lymphoma from integrated small B-cell morphology, lymphoepithelial lesions, and compatible immunophenotyping while avoiding diagnosis from CD20 alone.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: H. pylori eradication as initial treatment for localized gastric MALT lymphoma
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select H. pylori eradication as initial treatment for the classic localized low-grade presentation and preserve confirmation and response-reassessment boundaries.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Confirmatory gastric-emptying testing for suspected gastroparesis
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select four-hour solid-meal gastric emptying scintigraphy to document delayed gastric emptying after mechanical obstruction has been excluded.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Avoid routine prophylactic splenectomy in proximal gastric cancer
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Preserve the spleen during curative gastrectomy for proximal gastric adenocarcinoma when there is no greater-curvature invasion, direct splenic invasion, or suspected splenic-hilar disease.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: High-risk peptic-ulcer stigmata requiring endoscopic hemostasis
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Distinguish active spurting, active oozing, and a nonbleeding visible vessel from low-risk clean-base or flat-spot findings when deciding whether endoscopic hemostasis is required.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Endoscopic hemostasis modality selection for peptic-ulcer bleeding
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select an accepted definitive thermal or mechanical modality, recognize that epinephrine is never definitive monotherapy, and apply the conventional epinephrine-plus-definitive-modality pathway without making all monotherapies universally wrong.
For the approved completed-imaging distal-obstruction profile, select the constrained combined endoscopic tissue-evaluation plan without treating CA 19-9 as confirmation.

Recognize an adult clinical pattern that supports Graves disease: symptoms compatible with thyroid-hormone excess together with diffuse thyroid enlargement and characteristic eye or pretibial skin findings when present, without requiring every feature in every patient.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: TRAb diagnostic support for Graves disease
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Use TRAb as etiologic support for Graves disease when a patient already has biochemical thyrotoxicosis; distinguish thyroid function from cause and recognize that a negative TRAb result does not fully exclude Graves disease.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: RAI evaluation for recurrent Graves hyperthyroidism
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Recognize recurrent hyperthyroidism after antithyroid-drug withdrawal as a setting where RAI evaluation is a reasonable counseling option, while retaining surgery and antithyroid-drug treatment as preference-sensitive alternatives.
Recognize current pregnancy as a contraindication to RAI treatment for Graves disease while continuing appropriate endocrine and obstetric assessment without RAI during pregnancy.
Recognize current breastfeeding as a contraindication to therapeutic iodine-131 for Graves disease and recognize the pre-treatment counseling boundary for feeding the current child.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: RAI avoidance with active moderate-to-severe TED
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Generally avoid therapeutic iodine-131 in ordinary Graves treatment counseling when specialist assessment documents active moderate-to-severe thyroid eye disease.
Select abdominal ultrasound as the initial imaging study for a stable outpatient with recurrent symptoms compatible with uncomplicated gallstones.
Use compatible recurrent symptoms and uncomplicated ultrasound-confirmed gallstones to support elective surgical assessment and cholecystectomy counseling.
Choose observation and counseling for uncomplicated incidental gallstones in an asymptomatic adult without suspicious gallbladder features.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Noncontrast CT for unresolved suspected stone disease
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select noncontrast CT to resolve stone presence, location, and obstruction in a stable nonpregnant adult after indeterminate ultrasound.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Metabolic evaluation after recurrent kidney stones
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select stone analysis when available together with urine and blood metabolic assessment for prevention planning after recurrent confirmed stone disease.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Initial serology for suspected celiac disease
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select tTG-IgA with total-IgA context as a usual initial serologic assessment while a patient with compatible symptoms continues eating gluten.
Select upper endoscopy with duodenal biopsies as the usual confirmation step for an adult with compatible positive celiac serology and adequate IgA.
Recommend a gluten-free diet with dietitian support after celiac disease is confirmed in the completed diagnostic pathway.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Diagnostic colonoscopy after a positive FIT
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select diagnostic colonoscopy after a positive screening FIT while recognizing that the stool result alone does not diagnose colorectal cancer.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Histologic confirmation of a colorectal lesion
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Identify histologic examination of sampled lesion tissue as the confirming evidence after colonoscopy identifies a suspicious colorectal lesion.
Choose ferritin and complementary iron studies to determine whether iron deficiency explains established anemia without relying on a numeric threshold.
Recommend suitability assessment for upper endoscopy and colonoscopy in adult men or postmenopausal patients with otherwise unexplained confirmed iron-deficiency anemia.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: MRI characterization of a concerning extremity mass
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select dedicated extremity MRI before biopsy for a deep, enlarging, or ultrasound-indeterminate soft-tissue mass while recognizing that imaging does not prove sarcoma.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Specialist-planned biopsy of a suspicious soft-tissue mass
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Refer a suspicious extremity mass to an experienced sarcoma team for planned image-guided core biopsy that preserves the future surgical approach.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: FNA selection for a suspicious thyroid nodule
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select ultrasound-guided FNA after normal TSH and ultrasound findings meeting biopsy criteria in the scoped stable outpatient pathway.
Recognize that capsular or vascular invasion distinguishing follicular adenoma from carcinoma requires histologic evaluation rather than follicular cytology alone.
Use repeat serum calcium with intact PTH to establish the biochemical pattern before localization planning in the scoped stable outpatient pathway.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Surgical assessment for complicated primary hyperparathyroidism
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Recommend parathyroid surgical assessment for biochemically confirmed primary hyperparathyroidism with authored renal or skeletal complications.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Dynamic ultrasound after an equivocal inguinal-hernia examination
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select targeted dynamic groin ultrasound for the scoped stable patient with intermittent symptoms and an equivocal examination.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Elective planning for symptomatic inguinal hernia
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Recommend elective repair discussion and planning after a reducible inguinal hernia is confirmed in a patient with meaningful activity-limiting symptoms.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Clinical recognition of acute anal fissure
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Recognize an uncomplicated acute anal fissure from recent defecation-related pain, scant bleeding, and a superficial midline tear.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Initial conservative care for acute anal fissure
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select stool-regulating fiber, fluids, soft formed stools, and sitz baths as initial care for a typical uncomplicated acute fissure.
Select anoscopy to define local canal anatomy after an appropriate broader evaluation in a stable patient with suspected internal hemorrhoids.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Office banding for persistent internal hemorrhoids
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select office rubber-band ligation for uncomplicated bleeding or prolapsing internal hemorrhoids that persist after conservative care.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Upper endoscopy for persistent esophageal dysphagia
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select upper-GI endoscopy with appropriate esophageal biopsies for stable persistent esophageal dysphagia with a structural or mucosal concern.
Recognize Barrett esophagus from a sampled columnar esophageal segment with specialized intestinal metaplasia.
Select high-resolution esophageal manometry after adequate structural evaluation for persistent solids-and-liquids dysphagia with regurgitation.
Recognize achalasia from absent peristalsis and impaired esophagogastric-junction relaxation without relying on an unsupported numeric threshold.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Complete diagnostic biopsy of a suspicious pigmented lesion
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select complete diagnostic excision with narrow margins and adequate depth for a small accessible pigmented lesion concerning for melanoma.
Discuss sentinel lymph-node biopsy for pathological regional staging of intermediate-thickness clinically node-negative melanoma alongside definitive excision planning.
Select targeted ultrasound to characterize an uncertain superficial collection after benign breast excision.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Observation of an uncomplicated postoperative seroma
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Observe a small simple asymptomatic postoperative seroma without infection, wound tension, implant, or functional limitation.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Clinical recognition of chronic pilonidal sinus
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Recognize chronic pilonidal sinus disease from recurrent natal-cleft drainage and characteristic midline pits without a current abscess.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Off-midline closure planning for pilonidal disease
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Plan an off-midline closure when excision with primary closure has already been selected for chronic pilonidal disease.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Targeted ultrasound for suspected lactational breast abscess
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select targeted breast ultrasound for a persistent focal inflammatory breast mass during lactation.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Selected drainage of a lactational breast abscess
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Choose image-guided drainage with culture and individualized antibiotic care for a suitable uncomplicated lactational abscess while preserving feeding when contact precautions are met.
Select laryngeal visualization for persistent voice change after thyroid surgery.
Localize loss of high pitch and projection with preserved ordinary vocal-fold mobility to external superior laryngeal nerve and cricothyroid dysfunction.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Contrast swallow for suspected Zenker diverticulum
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select contrast swallow with fluoroscopy for a classic proximal pouch presentation.
Recognize a posterior mucosa-and-submucosa pouch above the cricopharyngeus as Zenker anatomy.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Resting ABI for suspected peripheral arterial disease
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select resting ankle-brachial index testing for classic stable claudication symptoms and examination findings.
Select supervised or structured exercise before invasive therapy for stable functionally limiting claudication after risk reduction is addressed.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Three-site skeletal assessment in asymptomatic primary hyperparathyroidism
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select lumbar-spine, hip, and distal forearm DXA for skeletal assessment after primary hyperparathyroidism is confirmed.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Age-based surgical assessment in asymptomatic primary hyperparathyroidism
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Recognize age under 50 years as an independent reason to discuss parathyroid surgery after confirmed asymptomatic disease.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: ACTH classification after confirmed endogenous Cushing syndrome
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select plasma ACTH to classify the cause after endogenous hypercortisolism is already confirmed.
Select adrenal imaging for the suppressed-ACTH branch of confirmed endogenous Cushing syndrome.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: MRCP duct assessment for an indeterminate pancreatic cyst
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Use MRI/MRCP to assess communication between an indeterminate pancreatic cyst and the main duct.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Preoperative cross-sectional staging for colon cancer
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select contrast-enhanced CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis before treatment planning for confirmed colon cancer.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Oncologic regional resection for colon cancer
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select resection of the tumor-bearing colon with its regional lymphatic drainage for localized resectable colon cancer.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Multimodal response assessment after rectal cancer treatment
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select combined digital rectal examination, endoscopy, and rectal-protocol MRI after neoadjuvant treatment.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Selected watch-and-wait after clinical complete response
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Recognize intensive-surveillance watch-and-wait as an acceptable nonsurgical option for a fully informed adherent patient with a clinical complete response in an experienced program.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Confirmatory vascular imaging after carotid duplex
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select confirmatory CT angiography after duplex suggests severe symptomatic carotid stenosis.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Endarterectomy assessment for severe symptomatic carotid stenosis
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select prompt carotid endarterectomy assessment with best medical therapy for a suitable patient with severe ipsilateral symptomatic stenosis.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Germline polyposis evaluation after diffuse adenomas
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select hereditary counseling and APC/MUTYH germline testing after colonoscopy establishes diffuse adenomatous polyposis.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: IPAA referral for uncontrolled rectal FAP burden
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select restorative proctocolectomy/IPAA referral when rectal adenomas cannot be controlled endoscopically and restoration is appropriate.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: MRI mapping for recurrent complex fistula
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select pelvic MRI to map recurrent complex fistula anatomy.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Sphincter-preserving staged planning for high fistula
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Choose loose-seton referral and staged sphincter-preserving planning for high transsphincteric anatomy.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Use a supplied cutaneous primary and confirmatory outside pathology to identify small-bowel melanoma as metastatic disease retaining the primary cancer's identity.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Interpret negative films after swallowing a bone
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Recognize that negative plain films and preserved breathing do not exclude a retained swallowed bone in a symptomatic esophageal context.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Refer confirmed sharp esophageal objects emergently
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Arrange emergency hospital therapeutic endoscopic care for a confirmed sharp esophageal foreign body rather than elective observation or routine clinic scheduling.
Plan continued antiretroviral treatment when feasible and coordinate unavoidable interruptions with the HIV team.
Recognize increased midazolam exposure with ritonavir or cobicistat and coordinate route-specific sedation planning.
Use quantitative neuromuscular monitoring rather than head lift, apparent strength or visual twitch count alone to assess recovery from blockade.
Identify rocuronium and vecuronium as the blockers selectively complexed by sugammadex rather than assuming universal relaxant reversal.
Recognize peristomal irritant injury by the leakage distribution and distinguish it from an infectious or ulcerative process.
Address noninfectious leakage-related dermatitis with appliance fit, a compatible skin-protection plan and ostomy-nurse follow-up.
Identify detachment at the sutured intestinal mucosa-to-skin junction rather than labeling every stoma wound as retraction or necrosis.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Care of limited superficial stoma separation
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Choose local ostomy care and close follow-up for small superficial separation with viable bowel, while reserving surgical escalation for complicated separation.
Identify gallbladder carcinoma confined to the lamina propria as T1a, distinguishing muscular invasion from in-situ disease.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Completely resected incidental T1a gallbladder cancer
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Avoid automatic radical re-resection after expert confirmation of completely removed margin-negative T1a gallbladder carcinoma.
Recognize Merkel cell carcinoma from an integrated cutaneous neuroendocrine pathology assessment rather than assuming every skin nodule is squamous cancer.
Refer an appropriate clinically node-negative Merkel cell carcinoma candidate for sentinel-node staging rather than equating a normal node examination with pathologic node negativity.
Identify the retrorectus mesh plane between rectus muscle and posterior rectus sheath in midline incisional hernia planning.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Fascial closure rather than mesh bridging
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Plan fascial-defect closure with mesh reinforcement in an elective midline incisional hernia expected to close without advanced release, rather than routine bridging.
Recognize subtotal cholecystectomy as a safe bailout option when the critical view cannot be obtained rather than dividing unidentified structures.
Classify subtotal cholecystectomy as fenestrating or reconstituting according to whether the remaining gallbladder is left open or closed.
Explain a documented gradual CO2 rise during uncomplicated pneumoperitoneum by systemic absorption of insufflated gas rather than assuming an unrelated acute catastrophe.
Relate increased airway pressure during evaluated pneumoperitoneum to cephalad diaphragm displacement and reduced respiratory compliance.
Localize weak shoulder shrug and trapezius-pattern shoulder droop after posterior-triangle neck surgery to spinal accessory injury.
Localize medial scapular winging on forward pushing after axillary surgery to the long thoracic nerve and serratus anterior.
Avoid routine abscess incision when examination shows diffuse nonpurulent inflammation without a focal collection.
Recognize rapid or extensive spread as exceeding the uncomplicated clinic abscess pathway.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Urgent disposition for a classic appendicitis pattern
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select prompt emergency-department evaluation for a stable outpatient with a classic concerning appendicitis presentation.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Recognition of an incomplete appendicitis pattern
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Maintain suspicion for appendicitis when progressive focal right-lower-quadrant findings are present despite an incomplete classic pattern.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Do not delay suspected appendicitis for unavailable testing
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Choose emergency-department transfer rather than delaying a concerning appendicitis presentation for unavailable CT or substituting plain X-ray.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Recognition of suspicious mammographic calcification patterns
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Distinguish suspicious calcification morphology and distribution from typically benign patterns without treating any isolated descriptor as a tissue diagnosis.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Recognition of suspicious mammographic mass morphology
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Recognize mass shape and margin combinations that are concerning on mammography while preserving the boundary that imaging morphology is not a tissue diagnosis.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Initial diagnostic imaging of a palpable breast mass at age 30 to 39
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select diagnostic mammography or tomosynthesis with targeted breast ultrasound for the scoped patient age 30 to 39 with a new palpable breast mass.
Distinguish stable biliary symptoms from warning features requiring emergency evaluation.
Arrange formal ultrasound-based evaluation for stable suspected gallstone disease without substituting plain radiography.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Fluid confirmation of suspected chylous ascites
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Confirm suspected chylous ascites through diagnostic fluid sampling rather than inferring fluid composition from CT appearance.
Recognize acute painful irreducibility with obstructive features as requiring emergency surgical-capable evaluation.
Use the relationship among a direct inguinal defect, Hesselbach's triangle, the inferior epigastric vessels, and the transversalis fascia to classify and locate the defect during open repair.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Elective referral for symptomatic reducible inguinal hernia
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select elective surgical referral for a stable adult with a symptomatic, readily reducible inguinal hernia and no urgent features.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Evidence boundary for inguinal-hernia watchful waiting
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Identify the selected adult population for whom watchful waiting with safety-net instructions is guideline-supported.
Recognize a hand laceration with an abnormal active-tendon examination as outside routine clinic closure.
Evaluate wound depth, contamination, foreign material risk, and distal structural function before routine closure.
Choose simple diverticulectomy for long, narrow, tip-limited disease and segmental ileal resection when an involved base extends into adjacent ileum.
Identify complete excision without a prescribed fixed-width margin as the benign phyllodes local-treatment target.
Distinguish observation after an isolated positive benign margin from circumstances suggesting residual or transected tumor.
Apply the approved borderline close-margin counseling categories.
Identify the counseling margin target for borderline phyllodes planning.
Recognize the usual hematogenous rather than nodal spread pattern in phyllodes counseling.
Apply the approved malignant close-margin counseling categories.
Identify the counseling margin target for malignant phyllodes planning.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: No routine axillary staging for phyllodes
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Avoid routine axillary staging when nodes are nonsuspicious.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Suspicious-node biopsy exception in phyllodes follow-up
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Identify image-guided needle biopsy before considering axillary dissection for a suspicious node.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Cross-sectional evaluation of postoperative abdominal swelling
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis as the initial broad cross-sectional study for the approved stable postoperative presentation.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Initial hospital management of postoperative chylous ascites
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Choose symptom-directed drainage, an appropriate fat-modified nutritional strategy, and inpatient monitoring for the approved large symptomatic postoperative leak.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Parenteral nutrition for prolonged postoperative ileus
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Initiate parenteral nutrition as nutritional support when severe postoperative ileus persists beyond seven days, mechanical obstruction has been excluded, and adequate oral or enteral nutrition remains infeasible.
Arrange incision and drainage in an appropriately equipped setting for a classic uncomplicated drainable abscess.
Route a stable adult with image-confirmed symptomatic gallstones and no urgent features to elective specialist evaluation.
Apply the CDC wound-category and vaccination-history matrix without using antibiotics as tetanus prophylaxis.
Identify that a postoperative patient with vomiting and progressive distension needs prompt surgical-team and hospital-capable evaluation rather than routine clinic treatment.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Early enteral nutrition after severe burn
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Begin enteral nutrition as soon as feasible within 24 hours for an adequately resuscitated patient with an extensive burn and no enteral contraindication.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Right thoracotomy exposure in thoracic trauma
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select right thoracotomy exposure for planned operative management of localized proximal or middle thoracic esophageal, intrathoracic tracheal, or azygos injuries while recognizing the resuscitative-incision boundary.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Concurrent IV vitamin K with PCC
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Recognize the approved paired IV vitamin K and PCC teaching point.
Recognize the documented VKA exposure and bleeding or urgent-intervention scope for this emergency teaching.
Identify the named procoagulant factors in the four-factor PCC teaching set.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Four-factor PCC selection for VKA reversal
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Identify four-factor PCC as the approved rapid VKA factor-replacement product.
Identify the approved rapid, concentrated, lower-volume PCC comparison with plasma.

fullClinicalMeaningRecords.displayName: Macroporous synthetic mesh after a controlled enterotomy
fullClinicalMeaningRecords.learningObjective: Select permanent macroporous monofilament synthetic mesh when proceeding with a selected single-stage ventral or incisional hernia repair after secure enterotomy repair, adequate source control, minimal contamination, and no gross spillage.
